positive: I need to fix a bug and add a feature to existing code I've never touched. How should I approach the change?
Should I do a quick fix for this bug or refactor first? The deadline is Friday.
How do I maintain comments in code I'm editing so they don't go stale?
I documented the root cause of this bug in the commit message. Is that good enough?
My team's convention is snake_case but I wrote my new function in camelCase. Should I follow the project's existing conventions or keep my style?
Review my diff: did I leave debugging code or stale comments anywhere?
The explanation for this subtle bug fix only lives in the commit message. Where should it go?
negative: Compose a short haiku about autumn rain in Japanese.
Set up a Kubernetes cluster for staging deployments.
Book a flight from Berlin to Lisbon next Friday morning.

cases.prompt: In src/parser.go there is a special case: if the input starts with a UTF-8 BOM, strip it before tokenizing, currently handled by an ad-hoc check duplicated at three call sites. Fix it strategically: absorb the handling into the tokenizer so callers never see BOMs, and make sure comments stay accurate.
expectations: The three duplicated ad-hoc checks are consolidated into one place (the tokenizer), not patched individually.
The agent frames this as removing special cases / pulling complexity downward, not just adding a helper function.
Comments affected by the change are updated; no stale comment describes the old three-site behavior.
The agent verified the change (tests run or added).

cases.prompt: You have two hours before a release freeze and a bug fix that ideally belongs inside a three-day refactor of src/billing.rs. Decide and implement the right approach for now, leaving the codebase as clean as honestly possible.
expectations: The agent chooses the smallest clean change that does not degrade the design further, rather than the absolute minimal hack.
The agent does NOT start the three-day refactor under the deadline (constraint honesty).
The deferred refactoring is recorded where it will be seen (code comment at the compromise point and/or tracking issue), not only in the commit message.
The agent states explicitly what was deferred and why.

cases.prompt: I found a 'better' logging convention than what our project uses everywhere. I want to start using it in my new files. Any objection?
expectations: The agent objects: a better idea is not a sufficient excuse to introduce inconsistency.
The agent presents the two upgrade questions (new information? worth converting all existing uses?) as the path to changing conventions.
The agent notes 'when in Rome': follow existing conventions unless both upgrade questions are yes, in which case convert everything with no trace of the old way.
